# Implementation Plan: Codex Agent Per-cwd `.mcp.json` Discovery

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-05-13, improved via second review round on 2026-05-13. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-mcp-discovery/plan.md`.*

> **Plan review status:**
> - **Round 1:** 11 findings (1 Critical, 4 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low) — all applied. See `plan-review-findings.json` (legacy).
> - **Round 2 (this revision):** 8 findings + 3 verification-driven info items (1 High, 4 Medium, 3 Low, 3 Info) — all applied. See the appendix at the bottom of this file and `plan-review-findings.json` for the manifest.

## Overview

The Claude agent under happy reads `<cwd>/.mcp.json` at session start (Claude Code's project-MCP convention), so a project that drops a `.mcp.json` in its repo root lights up automatically. The codex agent does not — `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.ts:700–705` builds the `mcpServers` object handed to `client.startThread({ mcpServers })` and to `resumeExistingThread({ mcpServers })` with **only** the `happy` bridge entry; project-level MCP servers (including `codexu`'s own `paper` HTTP server in the repo's `.mcp.json`) are silently dropped.

The fix lives entirely on the happy-cli side (codex submodule is unchanged): introduce a Zod-validated loader that reads `<cwd>/.mcp.json` at thread setup, validates each entry with a `command`-XOR-`url` superRefine, strips the Claude-style `type` field, merges the result into the object passed to both call sites, logs per-entry warnings on malformed or ambiguous input, and treats the `happy` bridge name as reserved. Four new sibling tests in `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/` exercise both the start and resume paths against mocked `client.startThread` / `client.resumeThread`. Roadmap, parallel-assignments, overview (with all six SKILL.md-mandated edits), parity audit doc, and the happy-cli `CLAUDE.md` open-gap entry are flipped to delivered in the same commit (with a single `--amend` after the initial commit to fold the resolved SHA into the `overview.html` `runs[]` and `generatedFromCommit` metadata).

### Technical Constraints

- **Schema must support BOTH transports.** The Claude shape `mcpServers` entries split by transport:
  - **stdio:** `{ command: string, args?: string[], env?: Record<string,string>, type?: 'stdio' }`
  - **http:** `{ url: string, type?: 'http' }` (no `command`)
  - The actual codex Rust `RawMcpServerConfig` (`codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs:190,274-325,312`) accepts `command` XOR `url` and **explicitly rejects cross-transport fields**.
- **Schema must enforce `command` XOR `url` via `superRefine`.** A naive `z.union([Stdio, Http]).passthrough()` accepts entries with BOTH because `.passthrough()` allows extras on each branch. Add an explicit `.superRefine((entry, ctx) => …)` (or per-branch refinement) that fails entries where both `command` and `url` are present, AND a helper unit test for the ambiguous case.
- **Codex `McpServerConfig` does not declare a `type` field.** The codex plugin loader strips it before deserializing (`codex/.../core-plugins/src/loader.rs:1042`). `RawMcpServerConfig` does not declare `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, so forwarding `type` is unlikely to crash, but stripping is the safer normalization and matches the upstream behavior. **Strip `type` after validation, before merging into the object passed to the codex client.**
- **Per-entry validation required.** A whole-object `z.record(McpServerSchema).safeParse(...)` would reject all entries on one bad entry. Spec requires "log + skip that entry — never abort the session" → iterate entries and `safeParse` each individually.
- **Reserved-name policy.** The `happy` bridge is platform infrastructure that the user did not opt into; if project `.mcp.json` defines a server named `happy`, log a warning and skip that single entry (do NOT let it override the bridge). 2-of-3 reviewer consensus (Codex, Copilot) from round 1.
- **Passthrough policy for extra Codex-supported fields.** `RawMcpServerConfig` supports `cwd`, `env_vars`, `http_headers`, `env_http_headers`, `bearer_token_env_var`, `startup_timeout_sec`, `tool_timeout_sec`, `enabled`, `required`, tool allow/deny. Use `.passthrough()` on the entry schema so unknown-but-codex-supported fields flow through verbatim. Validate only the well-known Claude-shape fields plus the XOR refinement; do not warn or strip passthrough extras.
- **Cwd snapshot semantics.** Capture `const cwdAtStart = process.cwd()` once, use it for **both** `loadProjectMcpServers(cwdAtStart)` AND the `cwd:` arg of `client.startThread` and `resumeExistingThread`. Avoids split risk if any future code or test calls `process.chdir()` between the load and the thread-start.
- **Reconnect is auto-handled by `rememberThreadDefaults`.** `codexAppServerClient.ts` `resumeThread` uses `opts?.mcpServers ?? defaults.mcpServers` (L1172) — the merged snapshot persisted on first `startThread` is reused on subsequent reconnects. The plan's snapshot-at-thread-start semantics naturally extend to reconnect without additional plumbing.
- **Single-commit + commit-SHA conflict.** `plans/overview.html` `runs[].commits` and `generatedFromCommit` require the landing commit SHA. Resolution: one initial commit containing all code+tests+docs (with `commits: ["pending"]` and `generatedFromCommit: "pending"` as sentinels), then a single `git commit --amend` to fold in the resolved SHA values. End-state is still a single commit at HEAD. Acceptance Criterion 9 documents this dance explicitly.
- **Roadmap/overview/assignments/parity-audit stay in sync.** Per `.agents/skills/roadmap-and-overview/SKILL.md`, status flips touch all four: `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`, `plans/parallel-assignments.md`, `plans/overview.html`, AND `plans/codex-agent-parity-audit.md`.

## Approach

### Architecture

Single-point fix in `runCodex.ts`: introduce a Zod-validated `loadProjectMcpServers(cwd)` helper that reads, parses, validates (including `command`-XOR-`url` superRefine), and normalizes `<cwd>/.mcp.json`. The helper returns an object suitable for direct merge into the existing `mcpServers` const, with the `happy` bridge name reserved and the `type` field stripped after validation. Both `startThread` and `resumeExistingThread` already read from the same local const → a single merge upstream of both consumers is enough. Reconnect is covered automatically by `rememberThreadDefaults` snapshot semantics.

### Implementation Strategy

1. **Create the loader module** `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/projectMcpConfig.ts`:
   - Zod entry schema is a union of two `.passthrough()` branches PLUS a `.superRefine` enforcing `command` XOR `url`:
     ```ts
     const StdioEntry = z.object({
         command: z.string(),
         args: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
         env: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional(),
         type: z.literal('stdio').optional(),
     }).passthrough();
     const HttpEntry = z.object({
         url: z.string(),
         type: z.literal('http').optional(),
     }).passthrough();
     const McpServerEntry = z.union([StdioEntry, HttpEntry]).superRefine((entry, ctx) => {
         const e = entry as Record<string, unknown>;
         if (e.command !== undefined && e.url !== undefined) {
             ctx.addIssue({
                 code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
                 message: '.mcp.json entry must have either `command` (stdio) XOR `url` (http), not both',
             });
         }
     });
     const McpRootSchema = z.object({ mcpServers: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()) }).passthrough();
     ```
   - Exported function: `loadProjectMcpServers(cwd: string): Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>` (sync — matches `codexAppServerDiscovery.ts` style).
   - Behavior:
     - File missing → return `{}` silently (no log).
     - JSON parse error → `logger.warn('[codex] .mcp.json parse failed', { path, reason })`, return `{}`.
     - Root shape invalid → `logger.warn('[codex] .mcp.json root shape invalid', { path, issues })`, return `{}`.
     - For each entry in `mcpServers`:
       - If entry name === `'happy'` → `logger.warn('[codex] .mcp.json: server name "happy" is reserved for the Happy bridge — entry skipped', { path })`, skip.
       - Run `McpServerEntry.safeParse(entry)`:
         - On failure (including superRefine XOR violation) → `logger.warn('[codex] .mcp.json server invalid', { path, serverName, issues })`, skip.
         - On success → strip the `type` field (Codex Rust `McpServerConfig` doesn't declare it; mirrors the codex plugin loader strip), accumulate into the result.
     - Return the accumulated normalized server object.

2. **Wire into `runCodex.ts`** at the existing `mcpServers` build site (L700–705):
   ```ts
   const cwdAtStart = process.cwd();
   const bridgeEntrypoint = join(projectPath(), 'bin', 'happy-mcp.mjs');
   const happyBridge = {
       command: process.execPath,
       args: ['--no-warnings', '--no-deprecation', bridgeEntrypoint, '--url', happyServer.url],
   };
   const projectMcpServers = loadProjectMcpServers(cwdAtStart);
   const mcpServers: Record<string, unknown> = {
       ...projectMcpServers,  // 'happy' already stripped by loader; `type` already stripped per entry; XOR enforced
       happy: happyBridge,    // platform bridge spread last → always wins (defense in depth on top of loader's reserved-name guard)
   };
   ```
   And use the same `cwdAtStart` for the `cwd:` arg of both `resumeExistingThread` (L724) and `client.startThread` (L791) — replace the inline `process.cwd()` with `cwdAtStart` in both call sites so load and thread-start agree on cwd in all cases.

3. **Tests** — two files, matching repo convention. **Both files** set `MockCodexAppServerClient.hasActiveThread = vi.fn(() => false)` and queue a user batch.
   - **`packages/happy-cli/src/codex/projectMcpConfig.test.ts`** — helper unit tests with `mkdtempSync` + `writeFileSync` fixtures. Each test creates and cleans its own tmpdir; `process.chdir` is NOT used (helper takes `cwd` as arg → no chdir needed). Cases:
     - Valid HTTP entry (`{ type: 'http', url: '...' }`) → returns one entry; `type` stripped; `url` preserved.
     - Valid stdio entry (`{ command: 'node', args: ['x'] }`) → returns one entry; `command` and `args` preserved.
     - Absent `.mcp.json` → returns `{}`, no log.
     - Malformed JSON → returns `{}`, warning logged with path.
     - Invalid root shape (e.g., `{}` with no `mcpServers` key) → returns `{}`, warning logged.
     - Mixed valid + invalid entries → returns only valid ones, one warning per invalid entry.
     - **Ambiguous entry `{ command, url }` (NEW)** → skipped with a warning citing the XOR-violation issue.
     - Entry name `'happy'` in project file → skipped with reserved-name warning.
     - Entry with extra Codex-supported fields (`http_headers`, `bearer_token_env_var`) → preserved verbatim via passthrough.
   - **`packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.projectMcp.test.ts`** — the 4 required acceptance tests against mocked codex client. Uses `process.chdir(tmpDir)` into a `mkdtempSync` directory; `afterEach` restores the original cwd; `MockCodexAppServerClient.hasActiveThread = vi.fn(() => false)`; a user batch is enqueued. **Fixtures use the HTTP shape matching the repo's actual `.mcp.json`:** `{ mcpServers: { paper: { type: 'http', url: 'http://127.0.0.1:29979/mcp' } } }`. **This file MUST NOT mock `./resumeExistingThread`** (unlike `runCodex.fork.test.ts`); the real forwarder must run so test (d) actually exercises `resumeExistingThread.ts:20–33` and the assertion is against the `client.resumeThread` mock.
     - **(a)** cwd with valid HTTP `.mcp.json` containing 1 entry → `client.startThread` mock called with `mcpServers` containing BOTH the `happy` bridge AND the project entry (with `type` stripped, `url` preserved).
     - **(b)** absent `.mcp.json` → `client.startThread` mock called with `mcpServers` containing ONLY `happy`.
     - **(c)** broken-JSON `.mcp.json` (concrete fixture: file contents `{ not valid json`) → `logger.warn` called AND `client.startThread` mock called with `mcpServers` containing ONLY `happy`. (Invalid-root-shape branch is exercised by the helper unit tests, not here.)

## Scope

### In Scope
- New `projectMcpConfig.ts` loader with Zod validation, stdio/http union, `.superRefine` XOR enforcement, `.passthrough()` for forward-compat, reserved-name guard, `type` strip.
- Edit `runCodex.ts` to call loader, merge with bridge-last spread, and use a single captured `cwdAtStart` for both load and call-site `cwd:` args.
- 4 acceptance tests (`runCodex.projectMcp.test.ts`) + helper unit tests including the ambiguous `{ command, url }` case (`projectMcpConfig.test.ts`).
- Roadmap, parallel-assignments, overview (with all 6 SKILL.md edits), codex-agent-parity-audit, and happy-cli CLAUDE.md doc updates.
- **One atomic commit at HEAD**, allowed to be created in two operations: initial commit with `"pending"` sentinels in overview.html SHA-bearing fields, then ONE `git commit --amend` to fold in the resolved SHA. The Acceptance Criterion 9 below documents this explicitly. The Preliminary Story Decomposition below is conceptual ordering for the implementer, NOT separate commits.

### Out of Scope
- **Primary codex integration test coverage** (`packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codex.integration.test.ts`). `packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md` states mocked tests do not count as acceptance for the codex agent. The feature request explicitly specifies mocked sibling tests as the deliverable for THIS change → followed as written. **Acknowledged follow-up:** a future task should add real-agent integration coverage of `.mcp.json` discovery to `codex.integration.test.ts`. This plan does not block on it.
- Upstream codex submodule changes (the Codex Rust app-server is intentionally left untouched).
- Generalization to other agents (gemini, openclaw) — the loader is structured for reuse but is wired only into the codex runner in this commit.
- Watching `.mcp.json` for changes after thread start (matches Claude Code's snapshot-at-start behavior).
- A `strictMcpConfig`-style toggle (Claude SDK option) — not in spec.
- Reconnect-path plumbing — covered automatically by `rememberThreadDefaults` (`codexAppServerClient.ts:1172`).

## Risk Areas

- **HTTP-only entries silently dropped (regression risk).** Round-1 Critical schema bug; resolved by union schema + HTTP fixtures.
- **Ambiguous entries forwarded as malformed (NEW, round 2).** `z.union(...).passthrough()` alone accepts `{ command, url }`. Mitigation: explicit `.superRefine` XOR check + dedicated helper unit test for the ambiguous case.
- **Codex `type` field forwarding.** Codex Rust `McpServerConfig` doesn't declare `type`; while `RawMcpServerConfig` lacks `deny_unknown_fields` (so it probably wouldn't crash), the canonical normalization is to strip. Mitigation: strip in the loader post-validation; explicit test assertion that `type` is NOT in the entry handed to `client.startThread`.
- **Reserved-name confusion.** If a project legitimately wants to publish a server called `happy`, we silently override their intent. Mitigation: explicit warning log naming the conflict and the bridge precedence policy. Defense in depth: bridge spread LAST in `runCodex.ts` so even if loader fails to filter, the merge still keeps the bridge authoritative.
- **Per-entry validation regression.** Easy to fall back to whole-object `safeParse` and break "skip the bad entry" requirement. Mitigation: explicit unit test for the "valid + invalid mix" case.
- **CWD split.** Loading from `cwdAtStart` but passing `process.cwd()` separately to thread-start could diverge if anything chdirs between. Mitigation: capture once, reuse for both load and call-site `cwd:` args.
- **`hasActiveThread()` skipping the test path.** `runCodex.fork.test.ts` sets `hasActiveThread = true`; if the new acceptance tests inherit that, `client.startThread` is never called and assertions never reach. Mitigation: explicit `hasActiveThread = vi.fn(() => false)` in the new test file.
- **Resume-path test masked by wrapper mock (NEW, round 2).** `runCodex.fork.test.ts` mocks `./resumeExistingThread` — copying that harness would prove the wrapper got `mcpServers` but NOT that the wrapper forwarded them to `client.resumeThread`. Mitigation: explicitly do NOT mock `./resumeExistingThread` in `runCodex.projectMcp.test.ts`; assert on `client.resumeThread` mock call args.
- **Test isolation.** Tests must `process.chdir` into a tmpdir (for the integration tests that exercise `process.cwd()` inside runCodex); failing to restore breaks subsequent tests. Mitigation: `afterEach` restoration of the original cwd; the helper unit tests in `projectMcpConfig.test.ts` pass cwd explicitly and avoid `chdir` entirely.
- **AGENTS.md acceptance-policy mismatch.** Repo policy says mocked tests don't count as acceptance for the codex agent; the feature request mandates mocked tests. Mitigation: documented in Out of Scope as an acknowledged follow-up.
- **Single-commit + commit-SHA-in-metadata conflict (NEW, round 2).** `overview.html` `runs[].commits` and `generatedFromCommit` need the SHA, which doesn't exist until the commit lands. Mitigation: explicit "initial commit with `pending` sentinels, then one `--amend` to fold in the SHA" workflow documented in Acceptance Criterion 9. End-state is still a single commit at HEAD.
- **Docs-flip miss (NEW, round 2).** `plans/codex-agent-parity-audit.md` was missing from the round-1 docs-flip list — addressed by adding it explicitly to Files to Modify.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Test (a) — valid HTTP `.mcp.json`, 1 entry, merge to startThread.** `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.projectMcp.test.ts` contains a test where cwd has a `.mcp.json` matching the repo's HTTP shape (`{ paper: { type: 'http', url: '...' } }`). The mocked `client.startThread` is asserted to have been called with `mcpServers` containing **both** the `happy` bridge AND the `paper` entry. The `paper` entry has its `type` field stripped; `url` is preserved.
2. **Test (b) — absent `.mcp.json`, only `happy` to startThread.** Same test file: cwd has no `.mcp.json`. The mocked `client.startThread` is asserted to have been called with `mcpServers` containing ONLY `happy`.
3. **Test (c) — broken-JSON `.mcp.json`, warning + only `happy` to startThread.** Same test file: cwd has a file `.mcp.json` whose contents are syntactically invalid JSON (concrete fixture: `{ not valid json`). `logger.warn` is asserted called (with a path-bearing payload) AND the mocked `client.startThread` is asserted called with `mcpServers` containing ONLY `happy`. (Invalid-root-shape branch is verified in the helper unit tests, not here.)
4. **Test (d) — resume path coverage.** Same test file: cwd has a valid HTTP `.mcp.json` AND the run is invoked with `opts.resumeThreadId` set. **`./resumeExistingThread` is NOT mocked**; the real forwarder runs. The mocked `client.resumeThread` is asserted to have been called with `mcpServers` containing BOTH the `happy` bridge AND the project entry.
5. **Helper unit tests.** `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/projectMcpConfig.test.ts` covers: HTTP entry (asserts `type` stripped, `url` preserved), stdio entry, absent file, malformed JSON, invalid root, valid+invalid mix (only valid kept, one warning per invalid), **ambiguous `{ command, url }` entry (logged + skipped per superRefine)**, reserved `happy` name (skipped with warning), passthrough of extra Codex-supported fields (`http_headers`, `bearer_token_env_var`).
6. **Vitest run is green.** `pnpm --filter '{packages/happy-cli}' exec vitest run 2>&1 | tee /tmp/codexu-mcp-disc.log` exits 0; all new tests pass; no existing test regresses. (If the implementer's shell lacks `/tmp`, a repo-relative log path such as `.ralph/jobs/codex-mcp-discovery/test-output.log` is an acceptable substitute — the original feature-request command stays canonical for traceability.)
7. **Cross-package typecheck is green.** `pnpm -r run typecheck` (or `pnpm --filter '{packages/happy-cli}' run typecheck` for the package alone, plus running typecheck across other packages that touch shared types) exits 0.
8. **Roadmap + parity audit + overview + assignments flipped.** All five doc artifacts updated as listed in Files to Modify, including all six SKILL.md procedure-B edits to `plans/overview.html`.
9. **Single atomic commit at HEAD, allowed to be created via initial commit + one `--amend`.** Workflow:
   - Run vitest + cross-package typecheck. Both must be green.
   - Stage all code+tests+docs (with `overview.html` SHA-bearing fields set to `"pending"`: `runs[].commits = ["pending"]`, `generatedFromCommit = "pending"`, kanban sub-text `(shipped pending)`, cmd-desc commit suffix `pending` if added).
   - `git commit -m '<message>'` — message references the roadmap bullet, e.g. `feat(happy-cli/codex): per-cwd .mcp.json discovery — closes codexu-roadmap "Codex agent project-.mcp.json parity"`.
   - Capture `SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)` and `ISO=$(git log -1 --format=%cI HEAD)`.
   - Edit `plans/overview.html` to replace the `pending` sentinels with the actual `SHA` and `ISO` values; also bump `generatedAt = ISO` and `runs[0].ranAt = ISO` if those were left as previous values during staging.
   - `git commit --amend --no-edit` — commit message unchanged; only the overview.html metadata diff is folded into the existing commit.
   - Verify: `git log -1 --format='%H %s'` shows exactly one commit with the SHA referenced in `overview.html` matching `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

**Note:** These are conceptual implementation slices for ordering, NOT separate commits — everything below lands in one atomic commit at HEAD (created via initial commit + one `--amend` per Acceptance Criterion 9).

- **US-001 (slice 1):** Loader module + helper unit tests (`projectMcpConfig.ts` + `projectMcpConfig.test.ts`), including the `superRefine` XOR check and the ambiguous-`{command,url}` test case.
- **US-002 (slice 2):** Wire loader into `runCodex.ts` (single `cwdAtStart`, merge, bridge-last spread) and add the 4 acceptance tests (`runCodex.projectMcp.test.ts`, including test (d) without mocking `./resumeExistingThread`).
- **US-003 (slice 3):** Doc updates: roadmap (`- ✅ ` prefix), parallel-assignments, overview.html (all 6 SKILL.md edits with `pending` sentinels), parity-audit, happy-cli CLAUDE.md (delete L236–258 bullet). Then run vitest + typecheck, create initial commit, `git commit --amend` with resolved SHA to fold into overview.html.
